title: RBAC v2 consistency verification, canary cutover, and audit reconciliation
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Migrate customers from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with a focus on data consistency, audit log parity, and SSO/SAML mapping correctness. Deliver a deterministic backfill, dual-write verification harness, and a conservative canary cutover that provides strong observability and automated reconciliation if drift is detected.
background: RBAC v2 introduces role-sets, domain-scoped policies, and canonical principal IDs. Prior migrations have uncovered parity issues in historical audit records and SAML assertion mapping edge cases. This ticket combines the engineering cutover checklist with a verification harness to prove correctness before wide release.
tasks: Implement 'rbac-v2-verify' job that compares effective permissions between v1 and v2 for a randomized sample of 10k accounts
Build audit-replay tool to transform RBAC v1 audit events into v2 canonical form and run hash parity checks
Create dual-write facade for 4 weeks: writes go to both v1 and v2 stores with deterministic conflict-resolution and write stamps
Add telemetry dashboards: per-tenant drift rate, permission-change diffs, SAML mapping failure rate, admin-ui toggle usage
Author customer communication templates and admin-facing FAQ for scheduled canary windows
Prepare DB backfill scripts: SQL and streaming backfill (names: backfill_rbac_v2_snapshot_v1.sql, stream_backfill_v2_consumer.py)
Implement retention-preserving audit migration to keep original event timestamps and chain IDs
Wire up SSO/SAML assertion test harness that replays sampled login events through v2 role mapping logic
Create canary cohort selection logic (0.5% of tenants first wave, 5% second wave) and automated gates
Run internal dry-run: simulate user workflows (token creation, role grant/revoke, resource access) against both systems and capture diffs
acceptance_criteria: Dual-write produces identical effective permission snapshots for >= 99.97% of sampled resources over 72-hour window
Audit-replay produces event-hash parity for > 99.9% of events after canonicalization rules
SAML assertion mapping test shows < 0.01% failures in canary tenants and no business-critical failures
Canary cutover automation can rollback to v1 within 15 minutes via feature flag and automated reconciliation
Monitoring dashboards surface drift and automatically open a JIRA/Linear incident when drift > 0.05% for 30m
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal dry-run on staging with production-sized data (2 weeks). Stage 2: Small canary (0.5% tenants) with dual-write for 72h, run verification suite and audit replay. Stage 3: Expand to 5% with extended monitoring for 7 days. Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 100% over 2 weeks with continuous reconciliation. Critical gate: no unreconciled drift > 0.02% in the last 24h at each ramp step.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: rbac_v2_drift_rate (percent) - alert if > 0.05% sustained for 30m
Metric: saml_mapping_failure_rate - alert if > 0.01% in canary cohorts
Dashboard: per-tenant drift heatmap, recent reconciliations, last-successful-backfill-id
Synthetic checks: weekly end-to-end permission validation for top 100 customers
cutover_checklist: Confirm dual-write facade deployed and telemetry flowing
Run initial rbac-v2-verify sample and record baseline hashes
Notify customers in canary cohort and post scheduled maintenance window
Enable admin UI 'RBAC v2 preview' toggle for selected tenants
Ensure on-call rotation includes security engineer and DB SME for first 48h
Verify automated rollback button works in console and triggers reconciliation job
backfill_strategy: Two-phase backfill. Phase A (fast snapshot): ingest current v1 state into v2 using bulk SQL with idempotent upserts and back-pressure. Phase B (streaming tail): consumer reads write-ahead-logs and applies incremental changes until dual-write window starts. Each batch produces a reconciliation token recorded in migration_log table. All operations are idempotent and emit audit entries linking to original v1 event IDs.
dual_write_strategy: Dual-write writes include 'source' tag and 'write_seq' monotonic counter. Conflict resolution favors highest write_seq per resource; a reconciliation pass resolves remaining conflicts by timestamp and manual review. There is a 'dual_write_probe' mode to compare writes without switching read traffic.
audit_log_verification_steps: Canonicalize v1 events: normalize actor IDs, resource URNs, and action names
Run audit_replay_tool on 30-day window and compute per-event hash using SHA256 canonicalization
Compare v1-hash to v2-derived-hash; log mismatches to reconciliation_queue with full payload
For mismatches, attempt deterministic repair: rewrite v2 event to canonical form and rerun hash
Escalate unresolved mismatches > 1000 events to security and compliance for manual audit
sso_saml_validation_steps: Collect representative SAML assertions from last 90 days (anonymized) and feed into saml-test-harness
Validate nameID formats, attribute mappings, and group-to-role translation rules in v2
Run cross-tenant test: sample enterprise tenants with custom mappings and confirm effective role results
Add automated unit tests for known edge cases (multi-value attributes, nested groups, IDP-specific quirks)
Document fallback mapping and admin overrides in the console for emergency remediation
admin_controls_changes: Add console toggle: 'Force RBAC v1 reads' for admins during cutover
Expose reconciliation status per-tenant in Admin > Security > RBAC Migration
Add one-click rollback action that triggers reconciliation and replays failed writes to v1
Audit-log all admin toggles and rollbacks with correlation IDs
Add role-level analytics: top granted permissions, last grant timestamp, grant origin (sso, api, ui)
qa_notes: Run acceptance suite against staging copy with synthetic tenants that exercise edge-case mappings
Include performance test: ensure RBAC v2 permission check adds < 2ms p50 latency per request
Validate audit log retention and downstream SIEM ingestion for sample customers
Coordinate with Solutions Eng for customer-specific mapping tests for top 20 customers
rollback_steps: Flip Admin toggle to force RBAC v1 reads for impacted tenants
Pause cron-based backfill and pause dual-write (enter read-only reconciliation mode)
Trigger reconciliation job that replays v2-stamped writes back into v1 if necessary
Open incident with runbook link and notify customers in the impacted wave
Post-rollback: run full permisssion-snapshot comparison and file RCA if drift > 0.05%
post_cutover_followups: Schedule 30-day audit of reconciled events and close-loop on any manual interventions
Deprecate dual-write facade after 4 weeks without incidents and archive migration logs
Create a postmortem if more than one rollback occurred or if customer-impacting drift exceeded thresholds
Update public docs and migration FAQ with lessons learned and common SAML fixes
